sanskrit: tac chrutvā sūtaputrasya vākyaṃ sāgaragāsutaḥ jahāsa sasvanaṃ hāsaṃ vākyaṃ cedam uvāca ha
english: Hearing those words of the sūta's son, the son of her who flows to the sea laughed aloud a ringing laugh, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: na hi tāvad raṇe pārthaṃ bāṇakhaḍgadhanurdharam vāsudevasamāyuktaṃ rathenodyantam acyutam
english: "Only because you have never yet met Pārtha in battle—bearing arrow, sword, and bow, joined with Vāsudeva, charging forward upon his chariot, that unfaltering one—

sanskrit: samāgacchasi rādheya tenaivam abhimanyase śakyam evaṃ ca bhūyaś ca tvayā vaktuṃ yatheṣṭataḥ
english: do you presume so, O Rādheya. For that reason you may go on boasting like this as much as you please."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etac chrutvā tu kaunteyaḥ sarvān bhrātṝn upahvare āhūya bharataśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing this, the son of Kuntī, O best of the Bharatas, summoned all his brothers aside in private and spoke these words.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainyeṣu ye cārapuruṣā mama te pravṛttiṃ prayacchanti mamemāṃ vyuṣitāṃ niśām
english: "The spies of mine who move among the armies of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son bring me this report, now that the night has passed:

sanskrit: duryodhanaḥ kilāpṛcchad āpageyaṃ mahāvratam kena kālena pāṇḍūnāṃ hanyāḥ sainyam iti prabho
english: Duryodhana, it is said, asked the son of the river, the man of mighty vows: 'In what span of time, O lord, could you slay the army of the Pāṇḍavas?'

sanskrit: māseneti ca tenokto dhārtarāṣṭraḥ sudurmatiḥ tāvatā cāpi kālena droṇo 'pi pratyajānata
english: 'In a month,' he was told; and the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra heard from Droṇa too that he would do it in just that span of time.

sanskrit: gautamo dviguṇaṃ kālam uktavān iti naḥ śrutam drauṇis tu daśarātreṇa pratijajñe mahāstravit
english: Gautama named twice that time, so we have heard; but Droṇa's son, knower of the great weapons, vowed to do it in ten nights.

sanskrit: tathā divyāstravit karṇaḥ saṃpṛṣṭaḥ kurusaṃsadi pañcabhir divasair hantuṃ sa sainyaṃ pratijajñivān
english: And Karṇa, knower of celestial weapons, being asked in the assembly of the Kurus, vowed to destroy the army in five days."

sanskrit: tasmād aham apīcchāmi śrotum arjuna te vacaḥ kālena kiyatā śatrūn kṣapayer iti saṃyuge
english: "Therefore I too wish to hear your word, Arjuna: in how great a span of time could you annihilate the foes in battle?"

sanskrit: evam ukto guḍākeśaḥ pārthivena dhanaṃjayaḥ vāsudevam avekṣyedaṃ vacanaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: Thus addressed by the king, Dhanaṃjaya, the thick-haired one, looked toward Vāsudeva and answered with these words.

sanskrit: sarva ete mahātmānaḥ kṛtāstrāś citrayodhinaḥ asaṃśayaṃ mahārāja hanyur eva balaṃ tava
english: "All these are great souls, accomplished in arms, varied in their fighting; without doubt, O great king, they could indeed slay your host.

sanskrit: apaitu te manastāpo yathāsatyaṃ bravīmy aham hanyām ekarathenāhaṃ vāsudevasahāyavān
english: Let the anguish of your mind depart; I speak to you in accordance with truth. With a single chariot, having Vāsudeva for my comrade, I could slay them—

sanskrit: sāmarān api lokāṃs trīn sahasthāvarajaṅgamān bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ bhaviṣyac ca nimeṣād iti me matiḥ
english: yes, the three worlds together with their gods, with all that is moving and unmoving, all that has been, that is, and that shall be—and in the blink of an eye, such is my conviction.

sanskrit: yat tad ghoraṃ paśupatiḥ prādād astraṃ mahan mama kairāte dvandvayuddhe vai tad idaṃ mayi vartate
english: That terrible and mighty weapon which the Lord of Beasts granted me in our single combat, when he wore the mountaineer's form—that very weapon abides in me.

sanskrit: yad yugānte paśupatiḥ sarvabhūtāni saṃharan prayuṅkte puruṣavyāghra tad idaṃ mayi vartate
english: That which the Lord of Beasts wields at the end of an age, O tiger among men, when he gathers in all beings—that very weapon abides in me.

sanskrit: tan na jānāti gāṅgeyo na droṇo na ca gautamaḥ na ca droṇasuto rājan kuta eva tu sūtajaḥ
english: That neither the son of Gaṅgā knows, nor Droṇa, nor Gautama, nor Droṇa's son, O king—and how then the son of the sūta?

sanskrit: na tu yuktaṃ raṇe hantuṃ divyair astraiḥ pṛthagjanam ārjavenaiva yuddhena vijeṣyāmo vayaṃ parān
english: But it is not right in battle to slay common men with celestial weapons; by fair fighting alone shall we conquer the foe.

sanskrit: tatheme puruṣavyāghrāḥ sahāyās tava pārthiva sarve divyāstraviduṣaḥ sarve yuddhābhinandinaḥ
english: And these tigers among men, your allies, O king, are all of them knowers of celestial weapons, all of them rejoicers in battle.

sanskrit: vedāntāvabhṛthasnātāḥ sarva ete 'parājitāḥ nihanyuḥ samare senāṃ devānām api pāṇḍava
english: All these unconquered ones, bathed in the final ablution of the Veda's culmination, could destroy in battle even the army of the gods, O Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī yuyudhānaś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ bhīmaseno yamau cobhau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau
english: Śikhaṇḍin and Yuyudhāna, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the grandson of Pṛṣata, Bhīmasena and the twins both, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas—

sanskrit: virāṭadrupadau cobhau bhīṣmadroṇasamau yudhi svayaṃ cāpi samartho 'si trailokyotsādane api
english: and Virāṭa and Drupada both, equal in battle to Bhīṣma and Droṇa; and you yourself are able even to wipe out the three worlds.

sanskrit: krodhād yaṃ puruṣaṃ paśyes tvaṃ vāsavasamadyute kṣipraṃ na sa bhaved vyaktam iti tvāṃ vedmi kaurava
english: The man upon whom you cast your gaze in anger, O you whose splendor equals Vāsava's, that man would swiftly cease to be—this is plain, and so I know you, O Kaurava."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prabhāte vimale dhārtarāṣṭreṇa coditāḥ duryodhanena rājānaḥ prayayuḥ pāṇḍavān prati
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, when the cloudless dawn had broken, the kings, urged on by Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son Duryodhana, set forth against the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: āplāvya śucayaḥ sarve sragviṇaḥ śuklavāsasaḥ gṛhītaśastrā dhvajinaḥ svasti vācya hutāgnayaḥ
english: All of them purified by bathing, garlanded, clad in white raiment, weapons taken up, standards raised, the blessing pronounced, the fires offered into;

sanskrit: sarve vedavidaḥ śūrāḥ sarve sucaritavratāḥ sarve karmakṛtaś caiva sarve cāhavalakṣaṇāḥ
english: all knowers of the Veda, all heroes, all of upright observances, all doers of the rites, and all bearing the marks of battle;

sanskrit: āhaveṣu parāṃl lokāñ jigīṣanto mahābalāḥ ekāgramanasaḥ sarve śraddadhānāḥ parasya ca
english: the mighty ones, seeking through battle to win the higher worlds, all of single-pointed mind, and full of faith in what lies beyond.

sanskrit: vindānuvindāv āvantyau kekayā bāhlikaiḥ saha prayayuḥ sarva evaite bhāradvājapurogamāḥ
english: Vinda and Anuvinda of Avantī, the Kekayas together with the Bāhlikas—all these set forth with the son of Bharadvāja at their head.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā śāṃtanavaḥ saindhavo 'tha jayadrathaḥ dākṣiṇātyāḥ pratīcyāś ca pārvatīyāś ca ye rathāḥ
english: Aśvatthāman, the son of Śaṃtanu, then Jayadratha of the Sindhus, and the warriors who came from the south, from the west, and from the mountains—

sanskrit: gāndhārarājaḥ śakuniḥ prācyodīcyāś ca sarvaśaḥ śakāḥ kirātā yavanāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: Śakuni the king of Gāndhāra, and those from the east and the north on every side, the Śakas, the Kirātas, the Yavanas, the Śibis, and then the Vasātis—

sanskrit: svaiḥ svair anīkaiḥ sahitāḥ parivārya mahāratham ete mahārathāḥ sarve dvitīye niryayur bale
english: all these great chariot-warriors, joined each with his own troops, surrounding the great chariot-hero, marched forth in the second division of the host.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā sahānīkas trigartāś ca mahābalāḥ duryodhanaś ca nṛpatir bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Kṛtavarman with his troops, and the mighty Trigartas, and King Duryodhana surrounded by his brothers;

sanskrit: śalo bhūriśravāḥ śalyaḥ kausalyo 'tha bṛhadbalaḥ ete paścād avartanta dhārtarāṣṭrapurogamāḥ
english: Śala, Bhūriśravas, Śalya, and then Bṛhadbala of Kosala—these moved in the rear, with the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra at their head.

sanskrit: te samena pathā yātvā yotsyamānā mahārathāḥ kurukṣetrasya paścārdhe vyavatiṣṭhanta daṃśitāḥ
english: Having advanced along a level road, those great chariot-warriors, ready to give battle, took their stand armored in the western half of Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu śibiraṃ kārayām āsa bhārata yathaiva hāstinapuraṃ dvitīyaṃ samalaṃkṛtam
english: Duryodhana then had a camp made, O Bhārata, adorned to be like a second Hāstinapura.

sanskrit: na viśeṣaṃ vijānanti purasya śibirasya vā kuśalā api rājendra narā nagaravāsinaḥ
english: Not even skilled city-dwelling men, O lord of kings, could tell the difference between the city and the camp.

sanskrit: tādṛśāny eva durgāṇi rājñām api mahīpatiḥ kārayām āsa kauravyaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Such strongholds, too, for the kings, the Kaurava lord of the earth had built by the hundreds and by the thousands.

sanskrit: pañcayojanam utsṛjya maṇḍalaṃ tad raṇājiram senāniveśās te rājann āviśañ śatasaṃghaśaḥ
english: Leaving clear a circle of five yojanas for the field of battle, the army's encampments, O king, filled it in their hundreds of companies.

sanskrit: tatra te pṛthivīpālā yathotsāhaṃ yathābalam viviśuḥ śibirāṇy āśu dravyavanti sahasraśaḥ
english: There those guardians of the earth, according to their zeal and according to their strength, swiftly entered camps well stocked with goods, by the thousands.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ duryodhano rājā sasainyānāṃ mahātmanām vyādideśa sabāhyānāṃ bhakṣyabhojyam anuttamam
english: For those great-souled ones, together with their armies and their attendants, King Duryodhana ordained provisions of food and drink beyond compare.

sanskrit: sagajāśvamanuṣyāṇāṃ ye ca śilpopajīvinaḥ ye cānye 'nugatās tatra sūtamāgadhabandinaḥ
english: For the elephants, the horses, and the men, and those who lived by their crafts, and the others who had come along there—the bards, the heralds, and the panegyrists—

sanskrit: vaṇijo gaṇikā vārā ye caiva prekṣakā janāḥ sarvāṃs tān kauravo rājā vidhivat pratyavaikṣata
english: the merchants, the courtesans, the harlots, and the people who came merely to watch—all these the Kaurava king looked after duly.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathaiva rājā kaunteyo dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhān vīrāṃś codayām āsa bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In just the same way the king, the son of Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Dharma, urged on the heroes led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: cedikāśikarūṣāṇāṃ netāraṃ dṛḍhavikramam senāpatim amitraghnaṃ dhṛṣṭaketum athādiśat
english: He appointed Dhṛṣṭaketu—leader of the Cedis, the Kāśis, and the Karūṣas, firm in valor, slayer of foes—as commander of the host.

sanskrit: virāṭaṃ drupadaṃ caiva yuyudhānaṃ śikhaṇḍinam pāñcālyau ca maheṣvāsau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau
english: Virāṭa and Drupada, and Yuyudhāna and Śikhaṇḍin, and the two great archers of Pāñcāla, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas—

sanskrit: te śūrāś citravarmāṇas taptakuṇḍaladhāriṇaḥ ājyāvasiktā jvalitā dhiṣṇyeṣv iva hutāśanāḥ aśobhanta maheṣvāsā grahāḥ prajvalitā iva
english: those heroes of brilliant armor, wearing burnished earrings, blazing like fires fed with ghee upon their altars—those great archers shone like flaming planets.

sanskrit: so 'tha sainyaṃ yathāyogaṃ pūjayitvā nararṣabhaḥ dideśa tāny anīkāni prayāṇāya mahīpatiḥ
english: Then that bull among men, that guardian of the earth, having honored the army each according to his due, commanded those troops to march.

sanskrit: abhimanyuṃ bṛhantaṃ ca draupadeyāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhān etān prāhiṇot pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Abhimanyu and Bṛhanta, and the sons of Draupadī all together, these led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna, the joy of Pāṇḍu sent forward.

sanskrit: bhīmaṃ ca yuyudhānaṃ ca pāṇḍavaṃ ca dhanaṃjayam dvitīyaṃ preṣayām āsa balaskandhaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Bhīma and Yuyudhāna and the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya—these Yudhiṣṭhira dispatched as the second wing of the army.

sanskrit: bhāṇḍaṃ samāropayatāṃ caratāṃ saṃpradhāvatām hṛṣṭānāṃ tatra yodhānāṃ śabdo divam ivāspṛśat
english: Of the warriors there loading the baggage, moving about and rushing to and fro, gladdened, the clamor seemed to touch the very heavens.

sanskrit: svayam eva tataḥ paścād virāṭadrupadānvitaḥ tathānyaiḥ pṛthivīpālaiḥ saha prāyān mahīpatiḥ
english: Then the lord of the earth himself, accompanied by Virāṭa and Drupada and the other guardians of the earth, marched in the rear.

sanskrit: bhīmadhanvāyanī senā dhṛṣṭadyumnapuraskṛtā gaṅgeva pūrṇā stimitā syandamānā vyadṛśyata
english: That army, moving with its dreadful bows, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at its head, appeared like the Gaṅgā in full flood, calm yet ever flowing on.

sanskrit: tataḥ punar anīkāni vyayojayata buddhimān mohayan dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putrāṇāṃ buddhinisravam
english: Then once more the wise one redeployed his divisions, baffling thereby the draining away of the wits of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sons.

sanskrit: draupadeyān maheṣvāsān abhimanyuṃ ca pāṇḍavaḥ nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca sarvāṃś caiva prabhadrakān
english: The sons of Draupadī, those great archers, and Abhimanyu, and Nakula and Sahadeva, and all the Prabhadrakas, the Pāṇḍava arrayed—

sanskrit: daśa cāśvasahasrāṇi dvisāhasraṃ ca dantinaḥ ayutaṃ ca padātīnāṃ rathāḥ pañcaśatās tathā
english: and ten thousand horses, and two thousand elephants, and ten thousand foot-soldiers, and five hundred chariots likewise.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ ca durdharṣaṃ prathamaṃ prādiśad balam madhyame tu virāṭaṃ ca jayatsenaṃ ca māgadham
english: And the unassailable Bhīmasena he assigned to the first force; in the center, Virāṭa, and Jayatsena the Māgadha;

sanskrit: mahārathau ca pāñcālyau yudhāmanyūttamaujasau vīryavantau mahātmānau gadākārmukadhāriṇau anvayātāṃ tato madhye vāsudevadhanaṃjayau
english: and the two great chariot-warriors of Pāñcāla, Yudhāmanyu and Uttamaujas, valorous, great-souled, bearing mace and bow—and then in the center followed Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: babhūvur atisaṃrabdhāḥ kṛtapraharaṇā narāḥ teṣāṃ viṃśatisāhasrā dhvajāḥ śūrair adhiṣṭhitāḥ
english: The men grew fiercely impassioned, their blows made ready; their banners, twenty thousand strong, were manned by heroes.

sanskrit: pañca nāgasahasrāṇi rathavaṃśāś ca sarvaśaḥ padātayaś ca ye śūrāḥ kārmukāsigadādharāḥ sahasraśo 'nvayuḥ paścād agrataś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: Five thousand elephants, and chariot-lines on every side, and the heroic foot-soldiers bearing bow, sword, and mace, followed by the thousands behind and by the thousands in front.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro yatra sainye svayam eva balārṇave tatra te pṛthivīpālā bhūyiṣṭhaṃ paryavasthitāḥ
english: Where in that ocean of force Yudhiṣṭhira himself was stationed, there for the most part those guardians of the earth took up their places.

sanskrit: tatra nāgasahasrāṇi hayānām ayutāni ca tathā rathasahasrāṇi padātīnāṃ ca bhārata yad āśrityābhiyuyudhe dhārtarāṣṭraṃ suyodhanam
english: There were thousands of elephants and tens of thousands of horses, and thousands of chariots and of foot-soldiers, O Bhārata, relying upon which he went to do battle with Suyodhana, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: tato 'nye śataśaḥ paścāt sahasrāyutaśo narāḥ nadantaḥ prayayus teṣām anīkāni sahasraśaḥ
english: Then others, by the hundreds behind, men by the thousands and tens of thousands, roaring as they went, marched on—their divisions numbering in the thousands.

sanskrit: tatra bherīsahasrāṇi śaṅkhānām ayutāni ca vādayanti sma saṃhṛṣṭāḥ sahasrāyutaśo narāḥ
english: There thousands of kettledrums and tens of thousands of conches were sounded by the men in their thousands and tens of thousands, exultant.
